```{python}
#| label: fig-ram-bist
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "RAM built-in self-test (BIST): a controller sequences a test-pattern generator and an address generator that exercise the RAM through multiplexers; the read-back data is checked in a comparator, yielding a pass/fail result. In mission mode, the multiplexers connect the RAM to the normal system inputs."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle, FancyArrowPatch


def box(ax, x, y, w, h, text, fc='#e8eef4'):
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x, y), w, h, fc=fc, ec='k', lw=1.0))
    ax.text(x + w / 2, y + h / 2, text, ha='center', va='center',
            fontsize=8.5)


def arr(ax, x0, y0, x1, y1):
    ax.add_patch(FancyArrowPatch((x0, y0), (x1, y1), arrowstyle='->',
                                 mutation_scale=11, lw=1.0,
                                 shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0))


fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.0))

box(ax, 0.2, 2.75, 2.6, 1.0, 'BIST controller', fc='#f4e8d8')
box(ax, 3.6, 4.2, 2.8, 0.9, 'pattern generator')
box(ax, 3.6, 2.8, 2.8, 0.9, 'address generator')
box(ax, 7.4, 2.8, 1.4, 2.3, 'MUX')
box(ax, 9.6, 2.8, 2.6, 2.3, 'RAM\nunder test')
box(ax, 9.6, 0.6, 2.6, 1.0, 'comparator')
box(ax, 3.6, 0.6, 2.8, 1.0, 'expected data')

arr(ax, 2.8, 3.25, 3.6, 3.25)
ax.plot([3.2, 3.2], [3.25, 4.65], 'k-', lw=1.0,
        solid_capstyle='projecting')
arr(ax, 3.2, 4.65, 3.6, 4.65)
ax.plot(3.2, 3.25, 'ko', ms=4)
arr(ax, 6.4, 4.65, 7.4, 4.65)
arr(ax, 6.4, 3.25, 7.4, 3.25)
arr(ax, 8.8, 3.95, 9.6, 3.95)
arr(ax, 10.9, 2.8, 10.9, 1.6)
arr(ax, 6.4, 1.1, 9.6, 1.1)
ax.plot([1.5, 1.5], [2.75, 1.1], 'k-', lw=1.0, solid_capstyle='projecting')
arr(ax, 1.5, 1.1, 3.6, 1.1)
ax.text(11.1, 2.2, 'read data', fontsize=7.5, rotation=90, va='center')
arr(ax, 12.2, 1.1, 13.1, 1.1)
ax.text(13.2, 1.1, 'pass/\nfail', fontsize=8.5, va='center')
ax.text(8.1, 5.6, 'normal system inputs', fontsize=8, ha='center',
        va='bottom')
arr(ax, 8.1, 5.6, 8.1, 5.1)

ax.set_xlim(0, 14.2)
ax.set_ylim(0.2, 6.0)
ax.set_aspect('equal')
ax.axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
